```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
# Keep the PNG extension so LaTeX does not substitute the older same-name PDF.
options(knitr.include_graphics.ext = TRUE)

cov <- read.delim("data/ncbi_flag_coverage_evidence.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
jun <- read.delim("data/ncbi_flag_junction_evidence.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
fsp <- read.delim("data/ncbi_flag_fullspan_evidence.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
cigar <- read.delim("data/ncbi_flag_cigar_audit.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
hits <- read.delim("data/review_blastp_span_besthits.tsv", check.names = FALSE,
                   quote = "", na.strings = "")
# Verify the internal best-hit summary against the original searches at render time.
span_genes <- read.delim("data/span_genes.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
for (arm in c("nr", "oomycota")) {
  path <- if (arm == "nr") "data/blastp_arm_unrestricted.tsv.gz" else
    "data/blastp_arm_oomycota.tsv"
  raw <- read.delim(path, check.names = FALSE, quote = "")
  raw <- raw[order(-raw$bitscore, raw$evalue, raw$sseqid), ]
  raw <- raw[!duplicated(raw$qseqid), ]
  expected <- raw[match(hits$query_protein, raw$qseqid), ]
  for (field in c("sseqid", "pident", "qcovhsp", "evalue", "bitscore"))
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(hits[[paste0(arm, "_", field)]],
                              expected[[field]], check.attributes = FALSE)))
}

contested <- c("MSU1_004_s1", "MSU1_004_s2", "MSU1_013_s1",
               "SC1982_008_s1", "OR502AA_015_s1", "OR502AA_022_s1")
bacterial <- c("SC1982_037_whole", "SC1982_071_whole")

cv <- cov[match(contested, cov$label), ]
bc <- cov[match(bacterial, cov$label), ]
expected_genes <- subset(span_genes, region == "span" & label %in% contested)
stopifnot(nrow(hits) == 59L, !anyDuplicated(hits$query_protein),
          setequal(hits$query_protein, expected_genes$protein_id),
          all(hits$label == expected_genes$label[match(hits$query_protein,
                                                     expected_genes$protein_id)]))
rep_hits <- hits[match(contested, hits$label), ]
for (i in seq_along(contested)) {
  rows <- hits[hits$label == contested[i] & !is.na(hits$nr_bitscore), ]
  rep_hits[i, ] <- rows[order(-rows$nr_bitscore, rows$nr_evalue,
                            rows$query_protein)[1], ]
}

# the junction counts quoted in the text are the 1 kb-overhang counts; confirm the
# two evidence tables agree before either is rendered
jl <- jun[jun$junction == "left",  ][match(contested, jun$label[jun$junction == "left"]),  ]
jr <- jun[jun$junction == "right", ][match(contested, jun$label[jun$junction == "right"]), ]
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(jl$span_1kb), as.integer(cv$left_junction_spanning_reads)),
          identical(as.integer(jr$span_1kb), as.integer(cv$right_junction_spanning_reads)),
          all(jl$span_1kb == jl$span_1kb_mq20),
          all(jr$span_1kb == jr$span_1kb_mq20))
cl <- subset(cigar, test == "left")
cr <- subset(cigar, test == "right")
cf <- subset(cigar, test == "full")
cl <- cl[match(contested, cl$label), ]
cr <- cr[match(contested, cr$label), ]
cf <- cf[match(contested, cf$label), ]
stopifnot(all(cl$coordinate_mq20 == jl$span_1kb_mq20),
          all(cr$coordinate_mq20 == jr$span_1kb_mq20),
          all(cf$coordinate_mq20 == fsp$full_1000_mq20[match(contested, fsp$label)]),
          all(cigar$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20 <= cigar$coordinate_mq20),
          all(cl$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20 > 0),
          all(cr$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20 > 0))

tt   <- function(x) sprintf("\\texttt{%s}", gsub("_", "\\\\_", x))
comma <- function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
kb   <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f kb", as.numeric(x) / 1000)
dx   <- function(x) sprintf("%s$\\times$", format(round(as.numeric(x), 1), trim = TRUE))

small_table <- function(df, col.names, align) {
  cat("\\begingroup\\small\n")
  print(knitr::kable(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
                     col.names = col.names, align = align, linesep = "",
                     row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\\endgroup\n")
}
```

To: genomes@ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

\vspace{1em}

Dear Colleagues,

Thank you for the contamination and genome-size reports. We have acted on part of the
contamination report and would like to ask you to reconsider the remainder. We also ask
that the genome-size alert be reassessed in light of the comparative evidence in Section
4: the synteny analysis across 15 oomycete genomes shows 1:1 correspondence rather than
duplicated blocks, and BUSCO duplication is low (3.16--5.45%), so we see no evidence
that these assemblies are haplotype-resolved --- the usual explanation for an assembly
exceeding its expected genome size.

**Accepted.** We agree with the two whole-contig bacterial calls in SC1982
(`Pcub-SC1982_037`, `r comma(517250)` bp; `Pcub-SC1982_071`, `r comma(118813)` bp; CFB
group bacteria). We accept their automatic removal by NCBI, as documented in the
FixedForeignContaminations report. Our read data support
these calls: the two contigs align at `r dx(bc$contig_mean_depth[1])` and
`r dx(bc$contig_mean_depth[2])` mean HiFi depth against a long-contig depth benchmark of
`r dx(bc$genome_median_depth[1])` --- about one sixth of that benchmark, consistent with
a lower-abundance co-isolated organism.

**Contested.** We ask that the six internal spans flagged as `fung:ascomycetes` (three in
MSU-1, one in SC1982, two in OR502AA) be retained. Each lies internal to a large host
contig. We request reconsideration based on read-alignment support, local coverage,
and the protein-homology results summarized below.

# 1. HiFi reads support every flagged boundary

We aligned the raw HiFi reads to the nuclear assemblies using minimap2 with the
`map-hifi` preset and `--secondary=no`, and retained primary alignments. Mapping was
performed against the full assembly before alignments on flagged contigs were extracted.
We then independently rechecked the existing BAM alignments, requiring mapping quality
$\ge$ 20 and at least 1 kb of aligned query bases on each side of a flagged boundary.
Only CIGAR operations M, =, and X contribute to the flanking-base counts. As a
conservative additional filter, we excluded any alignment containing a deletion or
reference skip of $\ge$ 50 bp anywhere in its CIGAR string. Counts below are distinct
read identifiers passing all these requirements.

```{r junction-table, results='asis'}
t1 <- data.frame(
  span   = paste0(tt(cv$label), " (", comma(cv$start), "--", comma(cv$end), ")"),
  len    = kb(cv$span_len),
  reads  = sprintf("%d / %d", cl$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20,
                              cr$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
small_table(t1,
  col.names = c("Span (coordinates)", "Length", "Left / right reads"),
  align = c("l", "r", "c"))
```

All 12 boundaries retain
`r min(c(cl$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20, cr$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20))`--`r max(c(cl$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20, cr$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20))`
supporting reads after this CIGAR-aware check. The original coordinate-only counts were
43--245; the stricter check removes a small number of alignments but leaves substantial
support at every boundary. Thus, the boundary support is not explained solely by
reference intervals spanning large alignment gaps. Mapping quality and these filters
cannot exclude every possible ambiguity, but together they strengthen the evidence for
physical continuity at the reported boundaries.

```{r fullspan-setup, include=FALSE}
fs <- fsp[match(contested, fsp$label), ]
a <- fs[fs$label == "MSU1_004_s1", ]
b <- fs[fs$label == "OR502AA_022_s1", ]
s <- fs[fs$label == "SC1982_008_s1", ]
stopifnot(all(fs$full_1000 == fs$full_1000_mq20))
```

The same CIGAR-aware criteria were applied to reads encompassing an entire flagged
region with at least 1 kb of aligned query sequence on each side. This retained
`r cf$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20[1]` reads for `r tt("MSU1_004_s1")`
(`r kb(a$span_len)`), `r cf$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20[6]` for
`r tt("OR502AA_022_s1")` (`r kb(b$span_len)`), and
`r cf$aligned_flanks_no_DN_ge50_mq20[4]` for `r tt("SC1982_008_s1")`
(`r kb(s$span_len)`). No full-region read met these criteria for the remaining three
spans, so their support rests on the individual-boundary alignments. Only the 52.2 kb
MSU-1 span exceeds the maximum read length recorded on its contig (45.2 kb); lack of a
full-region alignment for the other spans is an observation, not a read-length impossibility.

The assemblies were not scaffolded and the submitted sequences contain no N's. This
excludes scaffolding as the source of a join, but does not by itself exclude an
assembler misjoin; the read-alignment and coverage evidence are the basis of our request.

# 2. Coverage of the spans is consistent with the surrounding genome

We compared the median depth of each flagged span with its contig mean depth and the
median alignment-span depth among contigs at least 100 kb long. This long-contig
benchmark is not the median over all contigs. Similar coverage is consistent with host-genome
membership, although a co-isolated organism could coincidentally have a similar abundance.

```{r depth-table, results='asis'}
mk <- function(d, italic = FALSE) {
  v <- data.frame(
    span   = tt(d$label),
    sdep   = dx(d$span_depth_med),
    cdep   = dx(d$contig_mean_depth),
    gdep   = dx(d$genome_median_depth),
    ratio  = sprintf("%.2f", d$span_depth_med / d$genome_median_depth),
    zero   = ifelse(d$action == "exclude", "---", comma(d$span_zero_cov_bp)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (italic) v[] <- lapply(v, function(x) sprintf("\\textit{%s}", x))
  v
}
t2 <- rbind(mk(cv), mk(bc, italic = TRUE))
small_table(t2,
  col.names = c("Span",
                "\\shortstack[r]{Span\\\\depth}",
                "\\shortstack[r]{Contig\\\\mean}",
                "\\shortstack[r]{Long-contig\\\\benchmark}",
                "\\shortstack[r]{Span /\\\\benchmark}",
                "\\shortstack[r]{Uncovered\\\\bp}"),
  align = c("l", rep("r", 5)))
cat("\n\n\\begingroup\\footnotesize\\noindent",
    "Depth columns are median (span) or mean (contig) HiFi depth;",
    "The benchmark is the median primary-alignment reference span per contig base",
    "among contigs at least 100 kb long (35 MSU-1, 77 SC1982, and 48 OR502AA contigs);",
    "reference spans include CIGAR deletions and skips, whereas base-depth columns do not.",
    "The last two rows, in italics, are the whole-contig bacterial calls",
    "whose automatic removal we accept.\\endgroup\n")
```

Every contested span falls between
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(cv$span_depth_med / cv$genome_median_depth))` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(cv$span_depth_med / cv$genome_median_depth))`
of the long-contig benchmark, with no uncovered base. The two bacterial contigs removed by NCBI
provide an internal contrast at
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(bc$span_depth_med / bc$genome_median_depth))`--`r sprintf("%.2f", max(bc$span_depth_med / bc$genome_median_depth))`$\times$.
Thus, the contested spans have coverage more consistent with the surrounding genome
than with these two bacterial contigs. Coverage supports retention when considered
together with the alignment evidence, rather than serving as a taxonomic test on its own.

# 3. Protein homology and gene content of the flagged spans

We searched all `r nrow(hits)` predicted proteins overlapping the six contested spans
using DIAMOND blastp against nr, with an unrestricted search and a separate search
restricted to Oomycota (taxid 4762). Both used sensitive mode and an E-value threshold of
$10^{-3}$, retaining up to 250 and 25 target sequences per query, respectively. For each
protein, we selected the best reported hit by bit score, then E-value and accession.
Representative results are included below; full per-protein results are available on
request. A missing hit means no result was reported under these settings, not demonstrated
absence of a homolog.

```{r homology-summary, results='asis'}
nh <- vapply(contested, function(x) sum(hits$label == x & !is.na(hits$oomycota_sseqid)), 0L)
ng <- vapply(contested, function(x) sum(hits$label == x), 0L)
t3 <- data.frame(tt(contested),
  c("Hypothetical proteins", "Hypothetical proteins", "ERG3-like array",
    "ERG3-like protein", "ERG3-like protein", "Hypothetical / permease-like"),
  sprintf("%d / %d", nh, ng))
small_table(t3, c("Span", "Main sequence annotations", "Oomycota hits / genes"),
            c("l", "l", "c"))
```

The tables below show one representative query per span: the protein with the highest
unrestricted bit score in that span. The Oomycota table uses the **same queries**, so
its rows can be compared directly with the unrestricted results. Identity is the
percentage identity of the reported alignment, and coverage is the percentage of the
query covered by that HSP. Detection of a hit at the search threshold does not by itself
establish protein function or taxonomic origin.

```{r representative-hits, results='asis'}
esci <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "---", formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1))
for (arm in c("nr", "oomycota")) {
  cat("\n\n\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n")
  cat(if (arm == "nr") "\n\n\\noindent\\textbf{Unrestricted nr search}\\par\\smallskip\n" else
      "\n\n\\noindent\\textbf{Best Oomycota hits for the same representative proteins}\\par\\smallskip\n")
  get <- function(field) rep_hits[[paste0(arm, "_", field)]]
  species <- gsub(";", "; ", get("sspecies"), fixed = TRUE)
  tab <- data.frame(tt(rep_hits$label),
    ifelse(is.na(get("sseqid")), "---", tt(get("sseqid"))),
    ifelse(is.na(species), "---", species),
    ifelse(is.na(get("pident")), "---", sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", get("pident"), get("qcovhsp"))),
    esci(get("evalue")))
  cat("\\begingroup\\scriptsize\n")
  print(knitr::kable(tab, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c("Span", "Accession", "Species", "Identity / cov. (\\%)", "E-value"),
    align = c("l", "l", "p{3cm}", "r", "r"), row.names = FALSE, linesep = ""))
  cat("\\endgroup\n\\end{minipage}\\par\\medskip\n")
}
```

A dash denotes no hit meeting the search threshold. In `OR502AA_022_s1`, the
representative query has no reported Oomycota hit, but the other predicted protein in
that span does; hence the summary above reports 1/2 genes with Oomycota hits.

The representative ERG3-like proteins from MSU-1, SC1982, and OR502AA have high identity
to fungal proteins (`r paste(sprintf("%.1f", rep_hits$nr_pident[3:5]), collapse = ", ")`%,
respectively). Oomycota hits are also recovered, but they do not outweigh the stronger
fungal similarities or establish that the sequences are vertically inherited oomycete
genes. The MSU-1 contig 004 spans predominantly match a hypothetical protein from
*Plectosphaerella cucumerina*, whereas the representative protein from OR502AA contig
022 matches a permease-domain-containing protein from *Plectosphaerella plurivora*.
These affinities explain why the regions warrant scrutiny; the argument for their
retention rests principally on their read-supported genomic context.

Three spans, one per isolate, contain ERG3-like gene models together with a predicted
protein showing partial similarity to glutaminyl-tRNA synthetase. MSU-1 contains 38
ERG3-like models in the flagged region, compared with one in each of the corresponding
SC1982 and OR502AA spans. These are annotation-based counts, not experimentally verified
functional copies. The synthetase matches cover only 24.7--33.7% of the predicted query
proteins, so we do not assign a complete enzyme function on that evidence alone. This
recurring gene-content pattern is worth documenting, but we have not established
orthologous insertion sites by local flank-synteny analysis, and copy number alone
cannot exclude a fungal origin.

Wang et al. (2022) experimentally characterized an active ERG3 in the sterol-auxotrophic
*Phytophthora capsici*. This establishes that ERG3 can occur in a sterol-auxotrophic
oomycete, but does not establish its expected presence in *Pseudoperonospora*. Herzog et
al. (2020) reported repeated horizontal transfer of sterol C-5 desaturase genes among
Dikarya fungi. That study provides evolutionary context, not evidence of horizontal
transfer in our isolates. We have not reconstructed these gene phylogenies and do not
assign an evolutionary origin to the flagged regions here.

# 4. Genome size and comparative structure

We request that the assembly-size alerts be assessed together with the comparative
structure and gene-completeness evidence. The analysis across 15 oomycete genomes shows
that the three focal assemblies retain broad syntenic correspondence with related downy
mildew genomes and occupy the expected positions in the species tree (Figure 1).
The targetasm reassembly of the published *P. effusa* UA202013 reads also groups with the
published reference. These observations support taxonomic identity and conservation of
gene order in the assemblies.

Because the riparian plot is scaled by gene rank rather than physical sequence length,
we interpret it as supporting evidence for conserved genome structure, rather than as
an independent estimate of genome size. The assemblies used in this comparison recover
99.85--100% complete BUSCOs for the three focal isolates, with 3.16--5.45% duplicated
BUSCOs. An unmerged, haplotype-resolved assembly retaining both haplotypes of a diploid
genome would be expected to show substantially higher BUSCO duplication and duplicated
syntenic blocks in the riparian plot; we observe neither, so we find no evidence that
these assemblies are haplotype-resolved. This supports near-complete conserved gene space with limited duplication of
these markers, but does not exclude redundancy elsewhere in the assemblies. Differences
in repeat-rich and intergenic sequence can contribute to differences in assembly length;
we do not attribute all additional sequence to improved long-read resolution on the
basis of synteny alone.

# Request

We ask that the six internal `fung:ascomycetes` spans be retained on the combined evidence
of CIGAR-checked HiFi reads supporting every flagged boundary and span coverage
consistent with the surrounding genome. We acknowledge the fungal protein similarities
and distinguish these from the physical evidence supporting genomic membership. The
representative protein-homology results are presented above; full per-protein results,
underlying alignments, and per-base depth profiles are available on request. We also request reconsideration of the
assembly-size alerts in light of the comparative evidence and its stated limitations.

We accept only the two whole-contig removals listed above and request retention of all
remaining submitted sequences, including the six contested internal spans. We checked
the NCBI-modified SC1982 FASTA against the assembly used for read mapping: the two
bacterial contigs are absent, and all 473 retained sequences are unchanged in nucleotide
content. The supplied reports list no additional terminal contamination intervals.

Please do not automatically trim, mask, split, or exclude any additional sequence,
including sequence at contig ends, without first contacting us and obtaining our
confirmation. If further screening identifies additional putative contamination, please
provide the affected sequence identifiers, exact coordinates, and supporting screening
results for our review before making changes. Please confirm that no further automatic
sequence removal or trimming will be applied while this review is pending.

With thanks for your time and for the screen, which prompted a useful analysis.

\vspace{1em}

Sincerely,

Yixuan Yang, on behalf of the authors


# References

Wang, W., Cui, T., Zhang, F., Xue, Z., Zhang, B., and Liu, X. (2022).

[doi:10.3389/fmicb.2022.811132](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmicb.2022.811132).

Herzog, S., Brinkmann, H., Vences, M., and Fleißner, A. (2020).
Evidence of repeated horizontal transfer of sterol C-5 desaturase encoding genes among
dikarya fungi. *Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution*, **150**, 106850.
[doi:10.1016/j.ympev.2020.106850](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2020.106850).
